predator_rule: Pursue the prey while within predator vision; otherwise explore using the predator's own visited map. Local stuck recovery may briefly interrupt pursuit.
prey_rule: Avoidance has highest priority. When a visible predator is within predator_vision + avoidance_margin, evade until separation reaches that threshold plus avoidance_hysteresis. Otherwise pursue visible food, then explore. Thus the predator may remain inside prey vision without triggering continuous flight.
defaults_in_cells: Predator sees 24; prey sees 36. Prey start evading at 27 and stop at 30. Both maximum speeds are 18 cells/s. There are 12 cells per world unit.
avoidance_motion: Select a locally collision-clear waypoint prioritising separation from the visible predator; constrain intended evasion velocity to point away or sideways and use at least 80% throttle. Escape is attempted, not guaranteed after terrain collisions.
recovery_rule: Both organisms retain the two-second stuck rule and local escape waypoints. Prey recovery cannot override threat avoidance or cool down a predator. A newly dangerous predator interrupts non-avoidance recovery immediately.
memory: Separate visited maps, exploration targets and recovery/cooldown state per organism per encounter. No information about unseen opponents or unseen food is passed to either controller.
capture: Body contact ends the encounter; no respawn. Continuous capture follows collision-resolved piecewise movement paths. Capture takes precedence over pellet pickup during the capture timestep.
evolved: Separate 170-weight feedforward networks control steering offset and throttle under these programmed priorities. No role, vision, speed, target rule, memory map or recovery instruction evolves.
navigation: Shortest routes on four-neighbour body-clear terrain sites, cached reverse distance fields, and collision-clear waypoint smoothing. Both roles know static terrain but not unseen food/opponents. NN steering is redirected toward the route waypoint if its next step would hit terrain. Avoidance remains a local separation-first escape rule.
vision: Point line of sight to organism/pellet centres within the role vision radius. Solid terrain blocks detection. No last-seen opponent tracking. Vision outlines in replays are approximate 64-ray contours; sensor tests use exact segment collision.
